comparison: Perfect agreement on multivariate regression findings (C57-C61). Both evaluations find the statistical methodology appropriate and conclusions about host and viral characteristics well-supported by the data in Table 2.

Complete agreement on uncertainty regarding clonal expansion claims (C89-C92). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers note the data limitations, with peer reviewers specifically raising concerns about sequence homogeneity in hyperacute infection affecting interpretation. Both acknowledge authors' caution about this finding.

Full agreement on decay kinetics findings (C13, C94-C99, C128). Both evaluations affirm the differential decay rates between intact and defective genomes and between treatment groups, with appropriate statistical modeling and clear quantitative results from Figure 4.

Agreement on speculative nature of cure-related conclusions (C20, C130, C139-C140). OpenEval marks these as UNCERTAIN/SPECULATION while peer reviewers accept them as appropriately qualified future-oriented statements. Both recognize the claims are not directly tested but reasonably extrapolated from the data.

Strong agreement on longitudinal proviral DNA decline findings (C8-C9, C52-C56, C115). Both evaluations affirm the differential effects of treatment timing with appropriate statistical tests. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the more rapid decay with early treatment over one year.

Agreement on defective genome characterization (C70-C73, C77-C82, C123). Both evaluations support the quantitative data on defective proviral landscape. OpenEval also includes C11, C74-C76, and references to prior research (C37-C39) not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Agreement on reservoir establishment despite early ART (C7, C49, C113-C114, C137). Both evaluations support that early treatment blunts peak viremia but doesn't prevent initial seeding. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'starting treatment early didn't reduce the amount of HIV DNA at the outset.'

Partial overlap on early ART effects (C6, C48). OpenEval R2 addresses reservoir establishment despite early treatment, while peer R1 focuses on the broader finding that early ART links to reservoir kinetics. Both support the claims but emphasize different aspects.

Partial agreement on study design and population (C3-C5, C46-C47). OpenEval R1 focuses on methodological details while peer R10 emphasizes the novelty and importance of studying African women with subtype C. Both find these aspects well-supported.

Complete agreement on study population novelty (C135-C136). Both evaluations strongly affirm the importance of focusing on African women with subtype C infection, recognizing this addresses a documented gap in HIV reservoir research.

Significant disagreement on intact genome clearance (C12, C14, C83-C86). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of sampling limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that the 0% intact genome finding may reflect sampling depth rather than true absence, making interpretation problematic.

Agreement on CTL epitope and immune escape findings (C15, C132-C134). Both evaluations support the reduced immune escape with early treatment. OpenEval R10 provides more comprehensive coverage including C16, C104-C110 on protective HLA alleles and transmitted vs acquired mutations.

Partial overlap on sequencing and phylogenetic data (C63-C69). OpenEval R5 emphasizes comprehensive sequencing methodology and viral diversity differences (SUPPORTED), while peer R4 focuses on intact genome detection limitations (UNCERTAIN). Different aspects of the sequencing results are evaluated.

Minimal overlap on diversity findings (C66). OpenEval R5 addresses phylogenetic diversity from sequencing data, while peer R6 focuses on reduced diversity and immune escape. Both support reduced diversity with early treatment but from different analytical perspectives.

OpenEval R11 evaluates summary conclusions (C18-C19, C138) about decay kinetics, phylogenetic diversity, and CTL escape as SUPPORTED by comprehensive data. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these summary claims, though the underlying findings are evaluated elsewhere.

OpenEval R14 evaluates extensive background knowledge and literature review claims (C1-C2, C21-C45, C88, C93, C100-C101, C112, C116-C122, C126-C127, C129, C131) as appropriately cited. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual/background claims.

Minimal overlap on defective genome accumulation (C124). OpenEval R15 evaluates the inference about accumulation and comparison with prior studies as SUPPORTED though somewhat speculative. Peer R7 accepts the broader defective genome characterization without specifically addressing the accumulation inference.
